hero.headline: Zelensky warns of imminent major Russian attacks
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects a major attack from Russia within the next 48 hours based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours, citing intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies. Zelensky stated the attacks could come at night.

The warning comes as Ukraine continues to face military pressure from Russian forces.

cards.headline: Trump seeks changes to Iran deal negotiated by US envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump asked for several amendments to an agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting, according to a senior.
cards.body:
President Trump requested amendments to a framework agreement his envoys negotiated with Iran during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials. Trump wants to strengthen provisions related to Iran's nuclear material before approving the final deal.

The modifications have triggered another round of negotiations between the parties. The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Both sides appear committed to reaching a final deal, though the timeline for completing the revised version remains uncertain.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo kills more than 245 as aid agencies rush to respond
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 confirmed cases, with 246 suspected cases reported so far, according to health officials. The outbreak is centered in Ituri province, a conflict-affected region that borders Uganda and South Sudan.

The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate at between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases. "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die," said Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team.

Médecins Sans Frontières has described the spread of the virus as deeply alarming. The medical charity made this warning as the head of the World Health Organization arrived in the region to support containment efforts.

Uganda's health ministry has confirmed cases of the disease in the country. A 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC, marking the virus's spread across borders.

The outbreak poses particular challenges because Ituri province is a mining hub where thousands of people work in close proximity daily. The region is also affected by ongoing conflict between rebel groups. Displaced people are being forced into overcrowded camps to escape fighting, which makes controlling virus transmission significantly harder. These conditions create what experts describe as a perfect storm for disease spread.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed that the Ebola virus was detected in 13 of 20 samples tested. However, the detected strain is the Bundibugyo variant, for which there is no licensed vaccine. This differs from the more common Zaire strain found in previous outbreaks. Only two previous outbreaks of Bundibugyo have occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

Health workers in the region lack adequate equipment to contain the virus. Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia.

The Africa CDC director general, Dr Jean Kaseya, said the organization was convening an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the World Health Organization and pharmaceutical companies. "Given the high population movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries, rapid regional coordination is essential," he stated.

Aid organizations including MSF are rushing resources to the affected areas. Their response includes establishing treatment centers, distributing protective equipment to medical staff, and educating communities about infection prevention. International health authorities are working with Congolese officials to trace contacts of infected individuals and isolate new cases to prevent further transmission of the virus.

cards.headline: Eleven dead after chemical tank implosion at Washington state paper mill
cards.body:
Eleven workers died after a tank holding 900,000 gallons of corrosive chemicals imploded at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington. All bodies have been recovered and identified, according to local officials.

The tank implosion occurred at the mill facility, and experts say something went seriously wrong with the structure. The accident represents one of the deadliest industrial incidents in Washington state in recent years.

Longview officials worked to recover all nine workers initially reported missing, though the final death toll reached eleven. The discrepancy in numbers was not explained in initial reports.

The tank contained a large volume of corrosive chemicals used in paper manufacturing processes. The exact cause of the implosion remains under investigation, though industrial safety experts noted that such failures typically involve structural weakness or pressure irregularities.

Emergency response teams faced hazardous conditions due to the chemical content of the collapsed tank. The recovery operation required specialized equipment and protective measures to safely retrieve victims from the accident site.

The Nippon mill is a major employer in Longview, a city in southwestern Washington along the Columbia River. Paper manufacturing facilities use various chemical processes that require large storage tanks and specialized safety protocols.

Federal workplace safety investigators are expected to examine the incident to determine what led to the tank failure. Such investigations typically review maintenance records, structural inspections, and operating procedures.

The families of all eleven victims have been notified. Local officials have not released the names of those killed in the accident.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes at Florida Launch Site
cards.teaser: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded at its Florida launchpad hours after the company received a national security launch contract.
cards.body:
Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a test. The incident occurred at Launch Complex 36, just hours after the company received a national security launch task order from the U.S. government.

Blue Origin's CEO confirmed that the company has regained access to the damaged launchpad. The explosion was captured in aerial footage showing damage to the launch complex.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials, citing her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials, arguing that her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The filing was submitted to the U.S. District Court.

The recusal request centers on concerns that the judge's participation in the Willis event could create an appearance of bias in the case. The Justice Department's lawsuit involves Georgia election officials, and prosecutors argued the connection to Willis through the event could compromise the proceedings.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $87.5 Billion Investment in French AI Centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank will invest up to 75 billion euros to build what it calls Europe's biggest AI facility in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank has announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build artificial intelligence data centers in France. The project aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, positioning it as Europe's largest AI facility.

The investment underscores the intensifying competition among tech companies to expand computational infrastructure for AI development and deployment. France is becoming a major hub for these capital-intensive projects as global demand for AI computing power continues to surge.

cards.headline: Five rescued from flooded cave in Laos after being trapped over a week
cards.teaser: Rescue teams freed trapped villagers from a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week underground.
cards.body:
Rescue teams have freed five of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for over a week. The miners entered the narrow tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold before becoming stranded. The first person was rescued on Friday, followed by four more men extracted through hazardous conditions.

Divers have navigated treacherous passages filled with muddy water and sharp rocks to reach the trapped men. Rescue operations included draining water from the cave system and managing collapse hazards. Two people remain missing as rescuers continue their search through the deluged tunnels.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested as PSG Champions League celebrations turn violent in France
cards.teaser: Police arrested hundreds after celebrations of PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal led to clashes across French cities.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain retained their Champions League title after defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout, with Arsenal defender Gabriel missing the decisive kick.

The victory sparked celebrations across France that quickly turned violent. Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage crowds as fans took to the streets, with some firing flares during the festivities. Police made hundreds of arrests as unrest spread across multiple cities, with more than 130 people detained in Paris alone as officers worked to restore order.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers gave rare accounts of their experiences in Gaza, saying killings continue despite an announced ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to reporters describing military operations continuing in Gaza following the announced ceasefire. One soldier characterized the ceasefire as "a joke" given the persistent military activity on the ground.

An Israeli military commander told reporters that Hezbollah had developed plans for attacks similar to those carried out by Hamas. These soldier testimonies offer uncommon visibility into conditions and operations inside Gaza during the ceasefire period.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into Romanian apartment building as war threatens civilian areas
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war directly into civilian homes.
cards.body:
Residents of an apartment building in eastern Romania scrambled to return to their homes after a drone crashed into the structure early Friday morning, causing a blast and fire. The incident has left people living near Ukraine's border grappling with new fears about their safety.

The crash has intensified concerns among those in the region. Residents now face the stark reality that proximity to the Russia-Ukraine war poses real dangers to civilian populations, with many expressing that no one feels safe in their homes anymore.

cards.headline: Japan rejects claims of new militarism, points to Chinese military buildup
cards.teaser: Japan's defense minister dismissed Chinese accusations of new militarism, highlighting China's own rapid military expansion.
cards.body:
Japan's defence minister rejected Chinese accusations of pursuing new militarism, asserting that Japan remains a peace-loving nation. Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more assertive defence policy, moving away from its post-World War II pacifist stance with US support.

Japanese officials countered that China is expanding its military capabilities without sufficient transparency. The defence minister pledged to continue strengthening Japan's military despite Beijing's criticism of Tokyo's increasingly muscular security approach.

cards.headline: Iranian soccer team practices in Turkey while awaiting US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Iran's national soccer team remains in Turkey training for the World Cup as players wait for American visas.
cards.body:
Iranian soccer players continued practicing in Turkey while their visa applications to enter the United States remained pending. The team is preparing for the World Cup but faces uncertainty about whether they will be able to compete.

The players have developed backup plans as they wait for visa decisions. The delay overshadows their World Cup preparations and leaves the team's participation in doubt.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: The president asked for tougher terms after his negotiators reached a framework agreement with Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on an Iran nuclear deal after his negotiating team reached a framework agreement with Iran. The president requested edits to the terms before announcing a decision.

Defense Secretary Hegseth discussed the negotiations publicly, though Trump ended the meeting without announcing whether he would accept the framework agreement. The deliberation comes as the administration weighs the deal's terms.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump plans to renovate Kennedy Center and add his name
cards.teaser: A federal judge halted the president's proposed Kennedy Center closure and renovation, prompting an angry response from Trump.
cards.body:
A federal judge ruled that President Trump cannot add his name to the Kennedy Center and blocked his planned closure of the performing arts venue for renovations. The decision angered Trump, who vented publicly about the judge and his recent legal setbacks.

The ruling prevents the administration from moving forward with renovation plans that would have temporarily shut down the Washington cultural institution. Trump had proposed changes to the Kennedy Center that included adding his name to the building.

cards.headline: Trump in excellent health despite leg swelling and hand bruising, doctor reports
cards.teaser: The White House released results from the president's latest physical examination.
cards.body:
President Trump underwent a routine medical checkup at age 79, with results released by the White House. His physician, US Navy Captain Sean Barbabella, reported that Trump "remains in excellent health, demonstrating strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function."

The doctor's memo recommended that Trump lose weight and exercise more. Health assessments of US presidents are released publicly as part of routine medical checks, though experts note these reports often serve as much a messaging tool as a health evaluation.

cards.headline: Five killed in Virginia crash involving family traveling to wedding
cards.teaser: A bus driver faces charges after a collision that killed a family of four and one other person.
cards.body:
Five people died in a crash in Virginia, including a family of four who were traveling to a wedding. A bus driver has been charged in connection with the collision.

The family of four was among the victims killed in the accident. Authorities arrested the bus driver following the crash, though specific charges were not detailed in initial reports.

cards.headline: Four inmates escape from Alabama correctional center
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for four prisoners who broke out of a detention facility.
cards.body:
Four inmates escaped from an Alabama correctional center, prompting a search by law enforcement. The breakout occurred at a detention facility in the state.

Authorities have not released the names of the escaped inmates or details about how they fled the facility. A search operation is underway to locate and apprehend the four prisoners.

cards.headline: Becerra takes lead in California governor race poll
cards.teaser: The latest survey shows the candidate jumping ahead of competitors Steyer and Hilton before the primary.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra is leading in the Democratic primary race for California governor ahead of the June 2 primary election. The contest has tightened into a three-way race between Democrat Becerra, Democrat Tom Steyer, and Republican Steve Hilton.

The governor's race is part of a turbulent election cycle for California. Voters will eliminate all but two candidates in the primary, which also features competitive contests for Los Angeles mayor and several congressional races that could influence control of the US House. Californians head into the election with widespread frustration and dissatisfaction with the field of candidates.

hero.headline: Anthropic Raises $65 Billion, Surpassing OpenAI in Valuation
hero.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in its Series H funding round, bringing its valuation to $965 billion and making it more valuable than OpenAI. The funding round marks a significant shift in the competitive landscape of artificial intelligence development.

The seven cofounders of Anthropic are now worth a combined $116 billion following the funding round. The company's rapid ascent has positioned it as a leader in the AI industry, attracting substantial investor interest.

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives described Anthropic's growth as representing just the beginning of a broader AI rally. The funding round reflects continued enthusiasm among investors for companies developing advanced AI systems, despite ongoing questions about the economics of large language models and generative AI.

The new valuation places Anthropic ahead of OpenAI, which had been widely regarded as the dominant player in the AI sector. OpenAI gained widespread attention with the release of ChatGPT and has partnered closely with Microsoft, which has invested billions in the company.

Anthropic has focused on AI safety research alongside commercial applications. The company was founded by former OpenAI executives who departed to pursue what they described as a different approach to developing artificial intelligence systems.

The funding comes as competition intensifies among AI companies to develop more capable models and secure computing resources. Major technology companies and startups have raised tens of billions of dollars to fund AI development, driving up valuations across the sector.

The $965 billion valuation represents one of the highest for a private technology company. Investor appetite for AI companies has remained strong despite broader economic uncertainty, with backers betting that artificial intelligence will transform industries ranging from healthcare to finance.

The Series H round attracted participation from multiple investors, though the company has not disclosed the full list of participants or specific terms beyond the total amount raised and resulting valuation.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes at Florida Launch Site
cards.teaser: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded at its Florida launchpad hours after the company received a national security launch contract.
cards.body:
Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a test. The incident occurred at Launch Complex 36, just hours after the company received a national security launch task order from the U.S. government.

Blue Origin's CEO confirmed that the company has regained access to the damaged launchpad. The explosion was captured in aerial footage showing damage to the launch complex.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts Cockpit Breach
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger allegedly tried to breach the cockpit.
cards.body:
United Airlines Flight 2005 traveling from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison after a passenger attempted to access the cockpit. The incident triggered a hijacking alert and resulted in the arrest of the passenger.

The FBI announced it will not pursue charges against the 75-year-old passenger involved in the incident. The attempted breach forced the crew to divert the aircraft, described by officials as involving an unruly passenger.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $87.5 Billion Investment in French AI Centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank will invest up to 75 billion euros to build what it calls Europe's biggest AI facility in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank has announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build artificial intelligence data centers in France. The project aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, positioning it as Europe's largest AI facility.

The investment underscores the intensifying competition among tech companies to expand computational infrastructure for AI development and deployment. France is becoming a major hub for these capital-intensive projects as global demand for AI computing power continues to surge.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Weakens Further
cards.teaser: China's factory activity deteriorated in the latest data, signaling continued economic challenges.
cards.body:
Manufacturing activity in China worsened according to recent data, adding to concerns about the country's economic trajectory. The decline in factory output represents a warning sign for the world's second-largest economy.

The deteriorating factory performance comes as China faces multiple economic headwinds. Manufacturing data is closely watched as an indicator of broader economic health and global supply chain conditions.

cards.headline: New Car Sales Drop as One Million Buyers Exit Market
cards.teaser: The U.S. new car market has lost one million buyers, with sales declining for the eighth consecutive month.
cards.body:
Auto sales in the United States have fallen for eight straight months, with one million potential new car buyers disappearing from the market. Electric vehicle demand has collapsed as part of the broader downturn, according to industry reports.

Despite stagnating sales volumes, automakers continue to report profits. Analysts indicate the lost buyers are unlikely to return to the market soon, as new cars become increasingly unaffordable for many Americans.

cards.headline: Startups Offer Free Cleaning in Exchange for Filming Household Chores
cards.teaser: Technology companies are paying people to record themselves doing household tasks to train AI systems.
cards.body:
A startup is offering to clean apartments for free in exchange for permission to record the process. The filmed footage will be used to train artificial intelligence systems to recognize and potentially perform household tasks.

Multiple tech companies are seeking recordings of people doing chores, from washing dishes to organizing clutter. Workers are being paid to film themselves completing routine household activities, raising questions about privacy and the future of domestic automation.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, triggers sonic boom across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a powerful sonic boom that reverberated across the region. According to NASA, the blast was equivalent to 300 tons of TNT.

The fireball broke apart just after 2pm local time at an altitude of 40 miles, NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren confirmed. The meteor was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour when it fragmented in the atmosphere.

The explosion generated loud booms that were felt and heard across a wide geographic area. Hundreds of residents across New England reported experiencing the blast, with many taking to social media to describe their encounters. The sonic boom was so powerful that it rattled windows and startled people throughout the region.

Reports of the meteor came in from a broad area stretching from Delaware to Montreal, indicating the event was visible and audible across a substantial portion of the northeastern United States and into Canada. The geographic spread of sightings demonstrated the significant atmospheric disturbance created by the meteor's explosion.

Meteors explode when space rocks enter Earth's atmosphere at extremely high speeds. The friction and pressure from the atmosphere cause these objects to break apart. When they travel faster than the speed of sound, the resulting shock wave creates the sonic boom that residents hear and feel.

NASA explained that most space rocks smaller than a football field will break apart in Earth's atmosphere during entry. Though rare, some may explode in the air rather than reach the ground. According to scientific studies, approximately 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth annually.

The explosion over Massachusetts generated significant public attention, with numerous residents puzzled by the sudden boom and uncertain of its source until authorities confirmed the cause. Local media outlets reported extensively on the event as residents described their experiences and shared videos and photos of the incident.

Despite the dramatic nature of the explosion, no injuries or damage have been reported from the meteor event. Such atmospheric events occur periodically when meteoroids large enough to create significant disturbances enter Earth's airspace, though they remain relatively uncommon occurrences.

The incident highlights how visible and audible meteor explosions can be across large geographic areas when objects of sufficient size enter the atmosphere. The widespread nature of reports from this event demonstrated the scale of the atmospheric disturbance created by the meteor's fragmentation at high altitude.

cards.headline: First Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips to debut next week
cards.teaser: Microsoft and Nvidia will unveil the first Windows computers using Nvidia processors at an upcoming event.
cards.body:
The first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips will be introduced next week, according to Axios. The announcement will come during Nvidia's GTC event.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have all posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the reveal. The new processors, referred to as N1X laptop processors, represent Nvidia's entry into the Windows PC chip market. The development marks a significant shift in the personal computer industry, which has traditionally relied on Intel and AMD processors for Windows machines.

cards.headline: SoftBank commits up to $75 billion for French data center construction
cards.teaser: The Japanese firm plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in building data centers in France. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through this expansion.

The investment reflects growing demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure across Europe, positioning SoftBank to capture market opportunities in the region's digital economy.

cards.headline: James Bond game '007: First Light' sees strong sales in first 24 hours
cards.teaser: The new game combines elements of Hitman and Uncharted, according to reviewers.
cards.body:
'007: First Light' became a major sales hit in its first day of release, according to Mashable. Yahoo News Malaysia described it as the uncontroversial hit of 2026 with huge 24-hour sales figures.

The Verge called it the James Bond game fans have been waiting for. The New York Times compared the game to a mix of Hitman and Uncharted, while Game Informer praised its cinematic flair. The game's strong performance suggests renewed interest in the James Bond gaming franchise.

cards.headline: Rare blue moon visible this weekend
cards.teaser: The second full moon of May, a relatively uncommon occurrence, rises over the weekend.
cards.body:
A blue moon is the second full moon occurring within a single calendar month—a relatively uncommon event. Despite its name, the moon doesn't actually turn blue. This weekend's sky will feature this rare celestial occurrence, with favorable viewing conditions expected.

The phenomenon is even rarer this time, as it coincides with a micromoon—when the full moon appears smaller than usual. Viewers across the UK and beyond can observe this double rarity in the night sky this weekend.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus may help restore British habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: Scientists found a species that could control moss that has decimated native ecosystems.
cards.body:
A newly discovered fungus species offers hope for restoring native British habitats damaged by invasive moss. The fungus may be able to control the moss that has spread across vulnerable ecosystems.

The discovery raises the possibility that some native habitats could be brought back after being overtaken by invasive species. Researchers are studying how the fungus interacts with the invasive moss to determine its potential as a restoration tool.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backwards compatibility updates for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: The company issued a new wave of fixes to improve how original Switch games run on the newer console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released a new wave of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2. The updates address performance and functionality issues with older titles on the new hardware.

The fixes represent Nintendo's ongoing effort to ensure games from the original Switch console work properly on its successor. The company has been releasing periodic updates since the Switch 2 launched.

hero.headline: Spurs defeat defending champion Thunder to reach NBA Finals
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs advanced to the NBA Finals by defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory with 22 points and was subsequently named the Western Conference Finals MVP.

The win sends San Antonio to face the New York Knicks in the championship series, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. The matchup represents a rematch of the 1999 NBA Finals between the two franchises, which also met earlier this season in the NBA Cup final.

Wembanyama's standout performance throughout the series proved decisive in eliminating the Thunder, who had won the championship the previous season. The star player became emotional as the Spurs clinched their berth in the Finals, marking a significant moment in the team's postseason run.

San Antonio's victory marks their return to the NBA Finals for the first time since their last championship run. The Western Conference Finals went the full seven games before the Spurs emerged victorious, with the deciding contest played on the road against the defending champions.

The Spurs will face a formidable opponent in the Knicks, who are the Eastern Conference champions. Multiple sports outlets have published predictions and analysis examining the matchup between the two teams. Ticket prices for the Finals have been updated following the conclusion of the Western Conference Finals.

The Thunder came into the postseason as reigning NBA champions, but lacked Victor Wembanyama on their roster. The Spurs' star player proved instrumental in overcoming Oklahoma City in the conference finals series.

Wembanyama's individual award recognized his significant impact throughout the series against the Thunder. His 22-point effort in the closeout game exemplified his contributions across the playoff matchup as San Antonio advanced toward the championship.

The Spurs will look to capture another title with Wembanyama leading the way as they prepare for their Finals appearance. The team's return to the championship series represents a major accomplishment after eliminating last season's champions on the road in the deciding contest.

cards.headline: Hockey legend Claude Lemieux dies at 60
cards.teaser: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux has died at age 60, with his family announcing his brain will be donated for CTE research.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, has died at age 60. His family announced that his brain will be donated for chronic traumatic encephalopathy research.

Lemieux won four Stanley Cup titles during his NHL career. New details about his death have been revealed following the announcement. Close friends indicated he died of a broken heart for two deeply painful reasons, though specific circumstances were not detailed in available reports.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: French authorities arrested hundreds of people after Paris Saint-Germain fans fired flares and caused unrest celebrating their Champions League victory over Arsenal.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people were arrested in France following celebrations after Paris Saint-Germain retained the Champions League title, defeating Arsenal in a shootout. Thousands of police officers were deployed to control the unrest as crowds of PSG fans took to the streets.

Some fans fired flares during the celebrations as police worked to quell the disorder. The victory allowed PSG to achieve the rare feat of retaining back-to-back Champions League titles, while Arsenal's hopes of winning their first title in the competition were dashed.

cards.headline: Brighton manager Vidosic aims to honor late father in FA Cup final
cards.teaser: Brighton Women's manager Dario Vidosic hopes to honor his late father when his team faces Manchester City in the FA Cup final.
cards.body: Brighton manager Dario Vidosic is hoping to honour his late father when his team faces Manchester City in Sunday's Women's FA Cup final. The match represents a significant moment for Vidosic as he leads Brighton against one of English women's football's top teams in pursuit of the championship.

cards.headline: President Trump defends Giants quarterback Dart after rally appearance
cards.teaser: President Trump responded to criticism of New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart, calling critics jealous after Dart introduced him at a rally.
cards.body:
President Trump defended New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart against critics, calling them jealous. Dart had introduced the president at a political rally, sparking public disagreement.

Giants teammates Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter addressed the discourse surrounding the quarterback's rally appearance. Former NFL player Dez Bryant also defended Dart, saying he does not understand the hate from critics. Carter and Dart later expressed unity despite their initial disagreement over Trump.

cards.headline: Transgender California high school athlete wins state track medal
cards.teaser: Jurupa Valley senior AB Hernandez won a medal at the California state track and field championships amid protests over transgender athlete participation.
cards.body:
Transgender high school senior AB Hernandez from Jurupa Valley won a medal at the California state track and field meet. The athlete again topped qualifying scores at the CIF championships, which drew protests.

A press conference at the track meet involving the transgender athlete descended into chaos, with police summoned to the scene. Hernandez's mother spoke out as the championships drew demonstrations. Supporters of the trans athlete clashed with women's sports activists ahead of the state meet.

cards.headline: North Carolina defeats East Carolina 7-5 in NCAA baseball regional
cards.teaser: The North Carolina Tar Heels beat East Carolina 7-5 in the Chapel Hill Regional winner's bracket behind a three-run homer from Hynek.
cards.body:
North Carolina defeated East Carolina 7-5 in an NCAA baseball regional game. A three-run home run from Hynek sparked the Tar Heels past the Pirates in the Chapel Hill Regional.

The victory moved North Carolina through the winner's bracket of the regional tournament. In other NCAA tournament action, North Carolina State was eliminated, ending coach Elliott Avent's coaching run with the program.

hero.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be Reality TV Star Matt Brown After Apparent Suicide
hero.body:
Authorities have suspended the search for a man believed to be Matt Brown, a star of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, after reports that he took his own life. Brown's brother Bear Brown said Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

The 43-year-old reality television personality had appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed the Brown family living in remote areas of Alaska. Matt Brown was one of seven siblings featured on the show, which premiered in 2014 and ran for multiple seasons.

According to reports, a man matching Brown's description was seen near a river before going missing. Law enforcement officials have indicated they believe the individual may have taken his own life, leading to the suspension of active search efforts.

Bear Brown, Matt's younger brother and fellow cast member on the reality series, confirmed that Matt had been spotted in the area where the disappearance occurred. The family has not released an official statement regarding the situation.

Matt Brown had been open about his struggles in recent years. He left the show in 2018 to enter treatment and had discussed personal challenges publicly. The eldest of the Brown children, he had been a central figure in the series during its early seasons.

The Discovery Channel series followed the Brown family as they attempted to live off the grid in various wilderness locations. The show garnered a significant following for its depiction of the family's unconventional lifestyle and survival techniques.

Local authorities have not provided additional details about the circumstances of the disappearance or the decision to suspend the search operation. The investigation remains ongoing as officials work to confirm the identity of the missing individual and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour Over Health Concerns
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old music legend has canceled all remaining 2026 tour dates to focus on his health.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled the remainder of the Four Seasons farewell tour, citing health concerns. The 92-year-old singer announced he would be canceling all remaining 2026 concert dates to focus on his health, apologizing to fans for the disappointment.

Valli had been performing as part of a farewell tour with the Four Seasons, the vocal group he fronted for decades. The group became known for hits in the 1960s and remained a touring act for years. Valli's decision to cancel the remaining shows marks the end of the planned 2026 tour schedule.

cards.headline: Two YouTube Directors Behind Weekend's Top Box Office Films
cards.teaser: Horror films Backrooms and Obsession, both directed by filmmakers who started on YouTube, led the weekend box office.
cards.body:
The two highest-grossing films at the box office this weekend were both directed by filmmakers who began their careers on YouTube. The horror films Backrooms and Obsession topped the charts, with industry executives noting their success as a shift in how Hollywood discovers talent.

Jason Blum and James Wan discussed the phenomenon, with Blum comparing the current low-budget horror boom to the edgy films of the 1970s. Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca also weighed in on the success of the films, speaking at the Produced By conference hosted by the Producers Guild of America about the importance of pursuing new talent and fresh voices.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt's Son Maddox Files to Drop Actor's Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox Jolie-Pitt has filed to drop his father Brad Pitt's last name amid ongoing family tensions.
cards.body:
Maddox Jolie-Pitt, the son of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has filed to drop the Pitt surname from his legal name. The 25-year-old's decision comes years after his parents' separation and ongoing legal disputes.

Brad Pitt was photographed with girlfriend Ines de Ramon in Paris following news of his son's name change. Sources told Us Weekly that Pitt is hurt by his children dropping his last name and fears being permanently disconnected from them. The actor appeared to be in good spirits during the Paris outing despite the family tension.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Death of Former One Direction Bandmate Liam Payne
cards.teaser: The singer spoke about the loss of Liam Payne, who died in 2024 at age 31 after falling from a hotel in Argentina.
cards.body:
Niall Horan opened up about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at the age of 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said he was with Payne in Argentina just before his death. The singer described experiencing both sadness and moments of laughter when thinking about Payne because of the memories they shared together. One Direction was one of the most popular boy bands of the 2010s before the members pursued solo careers.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Second Cast Member in Two Years for Using Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery was dismissed from the upcoming season after social media posts surfaced showing her using the n-word.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed Vasana Montgomery from its cast after social media posts surfaced showing her using the n-word. Montgomery will no longer appear in the reality dating series, which returns to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year that the show has removed a cast member for the same reason. The announcement came just two days after the upcoming season was promoted. The series is produced for the streaming platform Peacock and follows the format of the international Love Island franchise.

cards.teaser: Hulu won two major categories at the 2026 CrimeCon Clue Awards announced over the weekend.

hero.headline: Zelensky warns of imminent major Russian attacks
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects a major attack from Russia within the next 48 hours based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours, citing intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies. Zelensky stated the attacks could come at night.

The warning comes as Ukraine continues to face military pressure from Russian forces.

cards.headline: Trump seeks changes to Iran deal negotiated by US envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump asked for several amendments to an agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting, according to a senior.
cards.body:
President Trump requested amendments to a framework agreement his envoys negotiated with Iran during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials. Trump wants to strengthen provisions related to Iran's nuclear material before approving the final deal.

The modifications have triggered another round of negotiations between the parties. The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Both sides appear committed to reaching a final deal, though the timeline for completing the revised version remains uncertain.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials, citing her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials, arguing that her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The filing was submitted to the U.S. District Court.

The recusal request centers on concerns that the judge's participation in the Willis event could create an appearance of bias in the case. The Justice Department's lawsuit involves Georgia election officials, and prosecutors argued the connection to Willis through the event could compromise the proceedings.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations released its annual report documenting sexual violence during armed conflict, adding Israeli and Russian security forces to its blacklist for the first time. The forces are among 77 government and non-government parties credibly suspected of systematic patterns of rape and other sexual violence in conflict zones.

The report includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians. The inclusion of both nations marks a significant milestone for the U.N. accountability mechanism, which tracks documented cases of sexual violence used as a weapon of war.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump in a social media post has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells has stepped down, according to a recent court filing. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina stated that Matthew Martin is no longer representing the government.

The indictment accused Comey of threatening Trump through the social media post, which has since been deleted. The prosecutor's departure comes as the criminal case continues to move through the federal court system in North Carolina.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to immigration detention center protests
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed New Jersey state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center after escalating protests.
cards.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center that has been the site of escalating protests. Sherrill and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin found common ground on the decision.

Sherrill said the New Jersey police officers have responded to protests taking place outside the facility. The deployment came after protests at the detention center intensified, prompting coordination between the state government and federal immigration authorities to address public safety concerns.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion fund for alleged weaponization targets
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion fund intended for people who claim they were targeted by government weaponization.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which was previously settled with a $1.8 billion fund. The decision came after a third-party motion challenged the settlement agreement, alleging it resulted from "collusion" and constitutes "a fraud on the court."

Judge Kathleen Williams issued the ruling that revives the original case Trump and his sons filed against the IRS following the unauthorized leak of their personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The reopened lawsuit will examine whether the anti-weaponization fund settlement meets judicial scrutiny.
